subject: BARGE
statement: The paper proposes BARGE, which employs Item Context-Aware Attention (ICA) to restore item-level structure during encoding.

subject: BARGE
statement: The paper proposes Hierarchical Path Reranking (HPR) together with Dual-Path Decoding (DPD) to suppress semantic drift during decoding.

subject: BARGE
statement: The paper reports an online A/B test on a Tencent platform yielding 0.60% improvement in click-through rate.

subject: BARGE
statement: The paper reports 1.70% improvement in total reading time from online A/B testing.

subject: RPMA
statement: The paper proposes a Regularized Projection Matrix Approximation (RPMA) framework for robust estimation of rank-K projection matrices.

subject: RPMA
statement: The paper develops a Riemannian gradient projection algorithm with backtracking line search to solve the nonconvex optimization problem.

subject: RPMA
statement: The paper demonstrates that RPMA substantially improves the recovery accuracy of projection matrices.

subject: RPMA
statement: The paper shows RPMA consistently outperforms conventional spectral projection methods for community detection and clustering under noisy environments.

subject: Faster IndexTTS-2
statement: The paper demonstrates up to 5.0x speedup on the autoregressive GPT component.

subject: Faster IndexTTS-2
statement: The paper reports 3.6x end-to-end speedup with minimal degradation in word error rate, speaker similarity, and naturalness.

subject: Faster IndexTTS-2
statement: The paper shows Faster IndexTTS-2 is 1.6-2.3x faster than Whisper.cpp at comparable model sizes (~1.6 GB).

subject: Experience Distillation
statement: The paper develops Experience Distillation, which internalizes contextual information from agent experience into model weights without further environment interaction.

subject: Experience Distillation
statement: The paper shows Experience Distillation retains at least 64.8% of the gains from in-context learning across both software-engineering and text-adventure domains.

subject: Experience Distillation
statement: The paper reports that in-context learning followed by Experience Distillation matches reinforcement-learning baseline performance with at least 9.6x fewer environment samples.

subject: QuantiBias
statement: The paper develops QuantiBias, a benchmark that pairs a generative, multilingual stereotype probe with refusal and multiple-choice controls.

subject: QuantiBias
statement: The paper finds that quantized models volunteer stereotypes in roughly one in four open-ended answers (~24% to ~27% across the compression ladder).

subject: QuantiBias
statement: The paper reports that quantizers allocate their extra precision by capability data that carries no bias-prevention signal.

subject: PrefReward
statement: The paper proposes PrefReward, a preference-aware generative framework that explicitly models user styles through a structured preference matrix.

subject: PrefReward
statement: The paper shows PrefReward outperforms non-personalized and retrieval-based baselines in both generation quality and personalization interpretability on the LongLaMP dataset.

subject: CounterFundus
statement: The paper presents CounterFundus, a novel CycleGAN-driven counterfactual explainability framework for retinal disease detection.

subject: CounterFundus
statement: The paper introduces the Counterfactual-Classifier Alignment Score (CCAS), embedding Spearman correlation, binary IoU and pointing accuracy.

subject: CounterFundus
statement: The paper demonstrates that CCAS-filtered counterfactual augmentation improves downstream classification performance in fundus images.

subject: GRPO
statement: The paper proposes reinforcement learning with a dense reward derived from the normalised ALPHA penalty for CWE prediction.

subject: GRPO
statement: The paper reports that the best policy reduces the cumulative ALPHA penalty of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on the SVEN dataset by 27.9% under greedy decoding.

subject: GRPO
statement: The paper reports 25.5% penalty reduction under sampled decoding (p = 0.005, Welch's t-test).

subject: SpecTraL
statement: The paper proposes SpecTraL, spectral transformation for layer-wise global rank discovery in federated LoRA for Vision Transformers.

subject: SpecTraL
statement: The paper performs orthonormal Householder Transformation of stacked adapters directly in the low-rank latent space.

subject: SpecTraL
statement: The paper demonstrates improved accuracy-communication trade-offs, reduced server computation, and elimination of hyperparameter search for rank selection.

subject: VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet
statement: The paper presents VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet, a compressed variant of VibeVoice-ASR optimized for real-time inference on edge CPUs.

subject: VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet
statement: The paper reports that VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet is 1.6-2.3x faster than Whisper.cpp at comparable model sizes (~1.6 GB).

subject: VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet
statement: The paper demonstrates real-time recognition with RTF < 1 using as few as 3 CPU threads.

subject: SOFT
statement: The paper proposes SOFT, a plug-and-play strategy that leverages the model's own one-step predictions to calibrate the biased input distribution.

subject: SOFT
statement: The paper demonstrates that SOFT achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-horizon forecasting tasks.

subject: SOFT
statement: The paper reports that SOFT substantially reduces both prediction errors and distributional discrepancy.

subject: adaptive splines knot selection
statement: The paper introduces a novel explicit knot-selection technique for GAMs based on an extension of the adaptive splines (A-splines) methodology.

subject: adaptive splines knot selection
statement: The paper demonstrates that the proposed approach produces models built on a substantially smaller number of basis elements.

subject: CASC
statement: The paper proposes CASC framework integrating a U-Net-inspired deep adversarial clustering architecture with stacked FAConvLSTM layers.

subject: CASC
statement: The paper proposes a Causal Subspace Preservation Loss that aligns self-expression coefficients with latent causal relationships.

subject: CASC
statement: The paper proposes a Dynamic Temporal Subspace Evolution Loss that captures evolving subspace structures and temporal regime transitions.

subject: RL self-explanation faithfulness
statement: The paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning method to directly optimize the faithfulness of self-explanations.

subject: RL self-explanation faithfulness
statement: The paper reports that RL fine-tuned Llama3.1-8B shows in-distribution Phi-CCT scores rising from near-zero to as high as 0.664.

subject: RL self-explanation faithfulness
statement: The paper reports out-of-distribution scores reaching up to 0.691 on held-out tasks such as StrategyQA.

subject: APEX
statement: The paper proposes APEX, a model-attribution co-design framework that makes the attribution integral exactly computable under polynomial GNN architecture.

subject: APEX
statement: The paper introduces PolyGIN, a GIN-style graph network whose message-passing operations preserve a bounded multivariate polynomial form.

subject: APEX
statement: The paper demonstrates that APEX achieves higher attribution fidelity than compared baselines while substantially reducing evaluation points.

subject: Smooth Neural Point Processes
statement: The paper proposes a novel neural TPP model that directly parametrizes the conditional intensity function as a non-negative combination of B-spline basis functions.

subject: Smooth Neural Point Processes
statement: The paper shows improved computational efficiency and predictive accuracy compared to the reference neural TPP baseline.

subject: semantic-ID cold items
statement: The paper shows that current SID-based models can occasionally reach future items supported by observed tokens and prefixes.

subject: semantic-ID cold items
statement: The paper reports that SID-based models struggle with unseen atomic tokens and unsupported SID paths.

subject: semantic-ID cold items
statement: The paper suggests that SID generation is compositional but not fully open-ended.

subject: AttriMem
statement: The paper proposes AttriMem, an attribution-guided process-feedback framework for learning memory-construction policies with RL.

subject: AttriMem
statement: The paper shows AttriMem outperforms retrieval-based, heuristic, and RL-based baselines on long-horizon dialogue question answering.

subject: AttriMem
statement: The paper reports that AttriMem generalizes across benchmarks and answer models, stabilizing RL optimization.

subject: TOUR
statement: The paper introduces TOUR, a benchmark combining trajectory-level partitioning, matched non-member controls, and multi-attack privacy auditing.

subject: TOUR
statement: The paper shows that common deletion baselines have environment-dependent privacy-utility behavior across D4RL locomotion experiments.

subject: TOUR
statement: The paper reports that a single likelihood-based membership score can overstate deletion quality.

subject: GlucoTune
statement: The paper presents GlucoTune, a comprehensive framework for reproducible experimentation with blood glucose time-series data.

subject: GlucoTune
statement: The paper provides standardized preprocessing workflows defined in portable YAML configuration files.

subject: GlucoTune
statement: The paper includes a benchmarking leaderboard that reports results across datasets, preprocessing configurations, and forecasting methods.
